What this means for an app

Most systems treat disagreement as a failure. An oracle that settles real money should expect it. Augur Lituus is built so that any answer can be challenged, and so that defending a wrong answer gets more expensive with every round.
One voice is a single point of failure

Smart contracts can’t see the world. Something has to tell them what happened, and whoever decides controls the money that depends on the answer. If that is one company, one committee or one multisig, the contract is only as honest as they are.
Anyone can answer, anyone can challenge

A reporter proposes an outcome and locks REP as a bond: a stake they can lose. The first answer is tentative, with time for others to check it. Anyone who disagrees can back a different outcome with a larger bond, and a completed challenge opens another appeal period.
Every challenge doubles the bond. A dispute that opens at 15 REP reaches 120 REP after three challenges, so it only continues while someone is willing to put more at stake on being right.
Figure 1. Each challenge doubles the bond: 15, 30, 60, then 120 REP.
Lying is designed to cost more than it pays.
What this means for an app
An application that settles on an Augur Lituus answer gets three properties from this design:
No committee, multisig or veto decides the answer.
Every answer is checked in public, under the same rules for everyone.
When an appeal period ends without a new challenge, the latest outcome becomes final.

If a dispute keeps escalating past a set threshold, it leaves the ordinary rounds and goes to a fork, the protocol’s last resort for the hardest questions. Forks are slow and costly by design, so ordinary disputes are meant to end long before one begins.

Ask, report, challenge, final answer: one example from start to finish.
Every Augur Lituus answer follows the same four steps. This guide follows one example question from the moment it’s asked to the moment an application can use the answer.
Has room-temperature superconductivity been independently demonstrated at ambient pressure?
Define what counts, when the question can be answered, and the possible outcomes. Pay a query fee in REP to request resolution.
A reporter proposes an outcome and locks REP as a bond: a stake they can lose. The first answer is tentative, with time for others to check it.
Anyone can back a different outcome with a larger REP bond. A completed challenge opens another appeal period. Disagreement follows the same public rules.
When an appeal period ends without a new challenge, the latest outcome becomes final. Applications can use that answer under their own settlement rules.

REP (Reputation) secures Augur’s oracle. Holders put it at risk to report outcomes and challenge wrong answers. It isn’t a passive asset: holding it comes with responsibilities.
Trading a prediction isn’t the same as reporting its outcome. REP is for reporting, challenging and, as a last resort, choosing a side in a fork.
Back an answer with a REP bond. If no one challenges it, it becomes final.
Disagree by posting a larger bond. If your answer holds, you win almost all of the losing bond.
If a dispute reaches a fork, holders move their REP to the universe they believe reflects reality.
Watch the protocol your REP belongs to and act during a fork, or you may miss its migration window. Rewards depend on taking part under each design’s rules; holding alone isn’t income.
